text.p: Here are highlights of stories in the Romanian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL
- State-owned bank Bancorex is expected to change its management this week, the newspaper says.

- More than 3,000 foreign companies registered in Romania have a share capital of $10, head of Romanian Development Agency, Andrei Dimitriu, told a news conference. He said only some 30 percent of 50,000 joint-ventures had a capital of $100,000 and more.
- Incomes in the building sector have doubled over the past year, while those of small retailers dropped by 15 percent.
- Banks attracted leu savings from the population, but it is unlikely that those funds will be used as credits, due to huge financial arrears in the economy and high interest rates.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Huge tracts of agricultural land will remain unploughed and unsown, due to lack of proper finance for the spring farming campaign, the newspaper says.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Romanian refineries must be privatised in order to be profitable, the newspaper says. Refineries should process an annual 18 million tonnes to become profitable.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Romanian parliament to debate later this week a bill to amend the 1991 land restitution law.
- Romania produces a total of some 360 million tonnes of waste annually of which 12 million tonnes is dangerous chemical waste.
- President Emil Constantinescu has started an official visit to the Czech Republic.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI

- Romania will face increasing difficulties with its Gypsy community in the coming 30 years, due to the poor literacy and high birth rate of the community, Party of Social Democracy senator Ion Solcanu said.
ADEVARUL
- The cost of funeral services can amount to 3.0 million lei ($387), while the average monthly wage is the equivalent of around $80.
CURIERUL NATIONAL

- Romania is the last European country without a national network for human transplants, due to low per capita income levels, which currently stand at $1,000 annually. ($= 7,744 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
